obligations.definition: The module top is a stateless combinational four-bit unsigned ALU with a decimal display selector. Inputs screen[1:0], opcode[2:0], A[3:0], B[3:0], and carry_in affect the outputs as specified below. There is no clock, reset or handshake. Compare outputs only after input changes have settled. All specified behavior applies to inputs containing only 0 and 1; behavior with X or Z inputs is unspecified.
obligations.setup: Drive all inputs to legal two-state values. No reset or preparatory state is required.
obligations.stimulus: Exercise all screen/opcode selections with changing operands and carry_in, repeated vectors, and transitions between modes. Observe after settling and verify that the same input produces the same output regardless of preceding inputs.
obligations.expected: The module top is a stateless combinational four-bit unsigned ALU with a decimal display selector. Inputs screen[1:0], opcode[2:0], A[3:0], B[3:0], and carry_in affect the outputs as specified below. There is no clock, reset or handshake. Compare outputs only after input changes have settled. All specified behavior applies to inputs containing only 0 and 1; behavior with X or Z inputs is unspecified.
obligations.sampling: Observe outputs after each driven input combination has remained stable long enough for combinational propagation in the declared simulator/time-unit context; do not compare outputs belonging to the previous vector. No particular nanosecond delay, hold duration, or duplicate sample count is required.
obligations.checker: Compute the relationships given herein independently from the inputs; do not read DUT outputs to generate expected values. Compare all specified outputs with the independent prediction in a valid settled window and report mismatches. Count comparison points and prohibit zero comparisons.

obligations.definition: screen=0 displays the unsigned opcode (0 through 7); screen=1 displays unsigned A; screen=2 displays unsigned B; screen=3 displays the selected ALU result. The displayed value is encoded as three packed BCD digits: bcd[11:8] is hundreds, bcd[7:4] tens, and bcd[3:0] ones. Each digit is 0 through 9 and leading zeros are retained. obligations.definition: When screen=3 and opcode=0, let S=A+B+carry_in using unsigned arithmetic. Display S modulo 16; carry_out=1 exactly when S is at least 16, otherwise carry_out=0. overflow equals carry_out in this mode: it denotes unsigned four-bit addition overflow, not signed two's-complement overflow. Both carry_in values are supported, including 15+15+1=31 (display 15, carry_out=1, overflow=1).

obligations.definition: When screen=3 and opcode=1, let D=A-B-carry_in using unsigned operands and treating carry_in as borrow-in. Display the nonnegative residue D modulo 16. carry_out is the borrow-out: it is 1 exactly when A is less than B+carry_in, otherwise 0. overflow=0. For example, 0-0-1 displays 15 with borrow-out 1, while 15-0-0 displays 15 with borrow-out 0.

Exercise all screen/opcode selections with changing operands and carry_in, repeated vectors, and transitions between modes. Observe after settling and verify that the same input produces the same output regardless of preceding inputs.
Cover explicit mode transitions and arithmetic or display boundaries. An exhaustive two-state sweep is sufficient; equivalent targeted coverage is accepted. No X/Z behavior is required.

coverage_policy: The fixed R obligations and five-dimensional denominator remain unchanged. All tests may be combined; stimulus cannot be supplied by inference from expected/given feature/names. Basic legal observable cases earn partial-domain credit; full credit requires satisfying both the complete domain and the boundaries. A locally invalid checker does not remove independent checker support already provided by other tests.
